Pessoa Digital

Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition titled "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa. What it edits, above all, are the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, set beside the works he published in his lifetime so as to trace the development of his oeuvre between planning and publication. The leesharks.com authorship census, which asks how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, admits it as an aggregator and holds it as a direct case in its area of heteronymy, asking how an edition holds Pessoa's own plans for his work, the lists and notes in which the names were assigned their works, beside what he published.

The CCeH's project page names its editors as Ulrike Henny-Krahmer (University of Rostock), Pedro Sepúlveda (Lisbon) and Jorge Uribe (Medellín), and its participants as the Laboratório de Estudos Literários Avançados (ELAB) of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa and the CCeH, where Ulrike Henny was responsible for the edition; for its other participants it refers to the edition's own team page. The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications". The two accounts name the Lisbon partner differently, a laboratory, ELAB, on the CCeH's page and an institute, IELT, on Rostock's, and the census follows the CCeH's. The edition is hosted by the DCH and supported by Portugal's Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT); for 2023 it received funding from the infrastructure project NFDI Text+, to make it more sustainable organisationally and technically and to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+. The surname of one editor is printed three ways across the two cards: Sepúlveda on both pages, Sepülveda in Rostock's account of the core team, and Sepúlvedo in the author line of the paper the CCeH cites.

Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe. A workshop and public lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, organised by the Akademie-Juniorprofessur Digital Humanities, presented its development and sustainability measures, with an evening lecture by Sepúlveda and Uribe Lozada on "Disjecta membra and restitution in Fernando Pessoa's self-publishing". The announcement gives Pessoa's dates as 1883–1935, where the CCeH's page gives 1888–1935 and English Wikipedia his birth on 13 June 1888.

The edition contains text transcriptions in TEI, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, and visualisations of its data as timelines and a network of persons, and it is built on an eXist database with XQuery and XSLT scripts and JavaScript. The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications. No saved source states its size, its licence or limits of its own, and how it marks the names under which Pessoa wrote, in its plans or its indexes, stays unread while its own pages refuse automated requests.

The census reads the edition as keeping the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned, a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, and sets that record beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions. Among the markers by which #940 tells a heteronym from a pseudonym is "A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively", and it holds that "A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself." On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns. Pessoa's own typology, from his letter to Adolfo Casais Monteiro of 13 January 1935, distinguishes orthonym, heteronym and semi-heteronym, and Teresa Rita Lopes and later critics extended it with the proto-heteronym and the para-heteronym; on the archive's typology, collapsing these distinctions treats his practice as "elaborate pseudonym". English Wikipedia gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own and states that he called them heteronyms, a term he invented, and it links the edition from its article on him as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa", with the words "and heteronyms". The edition's network of persons and the 2018 paper on the persons and figures of the publication plans stand beside the archive's reading that Pessoa's distinctive contribution is the system of heteronyms, their reciprocal relations and the master-disciple structure. #940's counter-principle holds that "The authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer": the civil bearer administers, publishes and answers for the work without becoming the exhaustive source of every authorial function operating through it, and the heteronymic architecture "ensures that the collapse registers as loss". It sets "Ordinary editing, where the editor's contribution is supportive rather than function-constitutive" outside heteronymy, names "Pessoa's Caeiro, Reis, Campos, and the constellation of heteronyms around them" in the tradition it joins, and plans a deposit on the heteronymic operation in the Pessoa archive as ethical practice.

The archive's essay on the meta-heteronym names a heteronymic system whose personae produce, besides literary works, the institutional apparatus, introductions, criticism, historiography and bibliography, under which those works become legible, and reads Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, incompletely. It counts Sepúlveda, with Jerónimo Pizarro, Teresa Rita Lopes and Richard Zenith, in the material turn that moved Pessoa criticism from text to archive, to the trunk, the 25,000 pages, the fragments and the unexecuted projects, and holds that "Se o meta-heterônimo é uma tecnologia institucional, o arquivo é a sua materialidade". It proposes that Pessoa's infrastructure, his editorial projects among it, be read as the meta-heteronymic operation in fragmentary execution, and gives as an instance the Tábua Bibliográfica of 1928, signed by the orthonym, which lists the heteronyms' works as works of independent authors. It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds.

#1722 holds that "A heteronym is a real author's practice: Pessoa wrote as Caeiro, Reis and Campos, and nobody concludes from this that Pessoa was a character", records a heteronymic practice, Pessoa's, read as a Sybil operation, answers that a heteronym is declared, its registry published with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and counts the heteronymous among those on whom the existence tax falls. It asks of an adequate answer that it name "the object at its own level".

The archive's Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers list Pessoa Digital among their primary-source reference archives, as a "critical digital editions project" beside the Biblioteca Nacional's Espólio and as a "digital editions project" in a list the working plan says to cite generously. They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.

The edition's own address answered the census's requests of 1 November 2026, for its home page and its about page, with HTTP 418 and a challenge page stating that "the administrator of this website has set up go-away to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites"; the census rests its row on the CCeH's page, supplied by the census's operator, and records the edition's own pages as unread. The challenge page's footer reads "Digital Humanities at the University of Cologne" and names the Cologne Center for eHumanities, the Data Center for the Humanities and the Department for Digital Humanities.

Wikipedia has no article under the name in English or Portuguese, and an English search for "Pessoa Digital" returns no page; English Wikipedia links the edition from its Fernando Pessoa article alone and lists Project Estranhar Pessoa there as a link of its own.

The census distinguishes it from the Arquivo Pessoa, a separate resource and its neighbour among the editions of Pessoa's work, which holds the published work under its names where Pessoa Digital holds the plans and lists.

On 1 November 2026 Google's AI Overview, asked "Pessoa Digital" at a new address, gave two senses, the edition first and second João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil and a distinct entity, from five cards: the CCeH's page, the Rostock announcement and three Instagram videos on the app, known here by their titles alone. The Capture Registry's innocent reading is that, given a two-word name shared by a scholarly edition and a city's services, the Overview gives both senses, the edition first, and asks which the user wants. The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed. It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.

Compression · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)Pessoa Digital

Pessoa Digital is the digital scholarly edition "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications" (pessoadigital.pt): Pessoa's notes, lists and plans for his work, edited beside what he published, the place where his works stand under their names before publication fixed them.

📜 What it edits

  • Object: handwritten notes, lists and plans, set beside the works published in his lifetime.4↘
    What it edits, above all, are the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, set beside the works he published in his lifetime so as to trace the development of his oeuvre between planning and publication.§2 On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns.§17 It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds.§26 The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed.§37
  • Holdings: TEI transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles; timelines and a network of persons.3↘
    The edition contains text transcriptions in TEI, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, and visualisations of its data as timelines and a network of persons, and it is built on an eXist database with XQuery and XSLT scripts and JavaScript.§12 The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications.§13 The edition's network of persons and the 2018 paper on the persons and figures of the publication plans stand beside the archive's reading that Pessoa's distinctive contribution is the system of heteronyms, their reciprocal relations and the master-disciple structure.§20
  • Unread: how it marks the names; its size, licence and limits.1↘
    No saved source states its size, its licence or limits of its own, and how it marks the names under which Pessoa wrote, in its plans or its indexes, stays unread while its own pages refuse automated requests.§14

🏛️ Makers

  • Editors: Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, Pedro Sepúlveda, Jorge Uribe; one surname printed three ways.5↘
    The CCeH's project page names its editors as Ulrike Henny-Krahmer (University of Rostock), Pedro Sepúlveda (Lisbon) and Jorge Uribe (Medellín), and its participants as the Laboratório de Estudos Literários Avançados (ELAB) of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa and the CCeH, where Ulrike Henny was responsible for the edition; for its other participants it refers to the edition's own team page.§4 The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications".§5 The surname of one editor is printed three ways across the two cards: Sepúlveda on both pages, Sepülveda in Rostock's account of the core team, and Sepúlvedo in the author line of the paper the CCeH cites.§8 The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications.§13 It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.§38
  • Partners: begun 2014 with the CCeH and a Lisbon partner (ELAB on one page, IELT on the other); launched 2017; EAFIT since 2019.7↘
    Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition titled "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa.§1 The CCeH's project page names its editors as Ulrike Henny-Krahmer (University of Rostock), Pedro Sepúlveda (Lisbon) and Jorge Uribe (Medellín), and its participants as the Laboratório de Estudos Literários Avançados (ELAB) of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa and the CCeH, where Ulrike Henny was responsible for the edition; for its other participants it refers to the edition's own team page.§4 The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications".§5 The two accounts name the Lisbon partner differently, a laboratory, ELAB, on the CCeH's page and an institute, IELT, on Rostock's, and the census follows the CCeH's.§6 Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe.§9 They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.§30 The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed.§37
  • Host and funding: the DCH; the FCT; NFDI Text+ for 2023.4↘
    The edition is hosted by the DCH and supported by Portugal's Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT); for 2023 it received funding from the infrastructure project NFDI Text+, to make it more sustainable organisationally and technically and to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.§7 Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe.§9 They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.§30 It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.§38

🧭 The archive's reading

  • Names: a heteronym's corpus is "produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively"; the plans hold that stage (#940; the census).3↘
    The census reads the edition as keeping the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned, a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, and sets that record beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions.§15 Among the markers by which #940 tells a heteronym from a pseudonym is "A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively", and it holds that "A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself."§16 On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns.§17
  • Function: attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer (#940).1↘
    #940's counter-principle holds that "The authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer": the civil bearer administers, publishes and answers for the work without becoming the exhaustive source of every authorial function operating through it, and the heteronymic architecture "ensures that the collapse registers as loss".§21
  • Meta-heteronym: Pessoa's editorial projects read as the apparatus in fragmentary execution; the category's test lies in the unexecuted projects (#69).3↘
    The archive's essay on the meta-heteronym names a heteronymic system whose personae produce, besides literary works, the institutional apparatus, introductions, criticism, historiography and bibliography, under which those works become legible, and reads Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, incompletely.§23 It proposes that Pessoa's infrastructure, his editorial projects among it, be read as the meta-heteronymic operation in fragmentary execution, and gives as an instance the Tábua Bibliográfica of 1928, signed by the orthonym, which lists the heteronyms' works as works of independent authors.§25 It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds.§26
  • Earlier description: the archive's graph papers call it "largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; its Cologne partner and Text+ funding contradict that.8↘
    Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition titled "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa.§1 The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications".§5 The two accounts name the Lisbon partner differently, a laboratory, ELAB, on the CCeH's page and an institute, IELT, on Rostock's, and the census follows the CCeH's.§6 The edition is hosted by the DCH and supported by Portugal's Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT); for 2023 it received funding from the infrastructure project NFDI Text+, to make it more sustainable organisationally and technically and to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.§7 Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe.§9 The archive's Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers list Pessoa Digital among their primary-source reference archives, as a "critical digital editions project" beside the Biblioteca Nacional's Espólio and as a "digital editions project" in a list the working plan says to cite generously.§29 They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.§30 The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed.§37

🔎 Reception

  • Access: its own pages answer automated requests with HTTP 418.1↘
    The edition's own address answered the census's requests of 1 November 2026, for its home page and its about page, with HTTP 418 and a challenge page stating that "the administrator of this website has set up go-away to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites"; the census rests its row on the CCeH's page, supplied by the census's operator, and records the edition's own pages as unread.§31
  • Wikipedia: no article; linked from Fernando Pessoa as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa".2↘
    English Wikipedia gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own and states that he called them heteronyms, a term he invented, and it links the edition from its article on him as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa", with the words "and heteronyms".§19 Wikipedia has no article under the name in English or Portuguese, and an English search for "Pessoa Digital" returns no page; English Wikipedia links the edition from its Fernando Pessoa article alone and lists Project Estranhar Pessoa there as a link of its own.§33
  • Overview: reaches it first of two senses, beside a Brazilian city's app; its object and editors dropped, its host misassigned (Capture Registry).3↘
    On 1 November 2026 Google's AI Overview, asked "Pessoa Digital" at a new address, gave two senses, the edition first and second João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil and a distinct entity, from five cards: the CCeH's page, the Rostock announcement and three Instagram videos on the app, known here by their titles alone.§35 The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed.§37 It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.§38

16the meta-heteronym: Pessoa's apparatus and editorial projects as institutional technology#69 O Meta-Heterônimo: Heteronímia como Tecnologia Institucional — Pessoa, · 2026-04-217 claims · #69
  • O69-01 #69 O Meta-Heterônimo: Heteronímia como Tecnologia Institucional — Pessoa, o Baú, e uma Leitura a Partir do Caso Pearl (2014 Rex Fraction (signed author); Lee Sharks (underlying heteronymic/submission identity) · 2026-04-21 · Resumo ¶1 s1 stipulation
    Este ensaio propõe a categoria do **meta-heterônimo** — um sistema heteronímico cujas personae não produzem apenas obras literárias, mas o próprio aparato institucional (apresentações, crítica, historiografia, bibliografia) sob o qual essas obras se tornam legíveis.
  • O69-02 #69 O Meta-Heterônimo: Heteronímia como Tecnologia Institucional — Pessoa, o Baú, e uma Leitura a Partir do Caso Pearl (2014 Rex Fraction (signed author); Lee Sharks (underlying heteronymic/submission identity) · 2026-04-21 · II, the material turn ¶ (para 51 of the string pass) s1 and s4 interpretation
    O **giro material** contemporâneo — Jerónimo Pizarro e sua equipe editorial, Teresa Rita Lopes, Richard Zenith como editor, Sepúlveda — deslocou a crítica pessoana do texto para o arquivo: o baú, as 25.000 páginas, os fragmentos, os projetos inexecutados (Pizarro, *Pessoa Existe?*, 2012). … Se o meta-heterônimo é uma tecnologia institucional, o arquivo é a sua materialidade.

1. Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa (pessoadigital.pt)

Pessoa Digital

Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", which the CCeH's page gives as a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa (1888–1935). It edits above all the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, juxtaposed with the works he published in his lifetime to trace his oeuvre between planning and publication. It contains TEI transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, timelines and a network of persons, built on eXist with XQuery, XSLT and JavaScript; a representative publication is "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018).

Its editors are Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, Pedro Sepúlveda and Jorge Uribe; it was begun in 2014 by a Lisbon partner, ELAB on the CCeH's page and IELT on Rostock's, with the CCeH, at the CCeH until 2016 and ongoing since. Its web presentation launched in 2017, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín began in 2019, and a core team led by Sepúlveda and Henny-Krahmer has developed it since, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its 2023 lecture. The editor's surname appears as Sepúlveda, Sepülveda and Sepúlvedo across the two pages. It is hosted by the DCH and supported by the FCT, and for 2023 NFDI Text+ funded it to make it more sustainable and integrate it into the Text+ research data infrastructure, the subject of a workshop and lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, one of them on Pessoa's self-publishing. Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013. Rostock's announcement gives Pessoa's dates as 1883–1935, against 1888–1935 on the CCeH's page and a birth in 1888 on Wikipedia.

Its own pages answered automated requests with HTTP 418 and a challenge page set up "to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites", its footer naming the University of Cologne's digital humanities units. Wikipedia has no article under its name; English Wikipedia's Fernando Pessoa article links it as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa" "and heteronyms", lists Project Estranhar Pessoa separately and gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own, which he called heteronyms. Three cards at the name concern João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil.

Compression · The field's ontology — L_F(B)Pessoa Digital

Pessoa Digital is the digital scholarly edition "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications" (pessoadigital.pt), a digital edition of Pessoa's editorial projects and publications: his notes, lists and plans beside his published works.

📜 Holdings

  • Contents: TEI transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, a network of persons.1↘
    It contains TEI transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, timelines and a network of persons, built on eXist with XQuery, XSLT and JavaScript; a representative publication is "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018).§3

🏛️ Makers

  • Editors: Henny-Krahmer, Sepúlveda, Uribe; begun 2014 with the CCeH and a Lisbon partner; launched 2017.4↘
    Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", which the CCeH's page gives as a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa (1888–1935).§1 Its editors are Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, Pedro Sepúlveda and Jorge Uribe; it was begun in 2014 by a Lisbon partner, ELAB on the CCeH's page and IELT on Rostock's, with the CCeH, at the CCeH until 2016 and ongoing since.§4 Its web presentation launched in 2017, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín began in 2019, and a core team led by Sepúlveda and Henny-Krahmer has developed it since, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its 2023 lecture.§5 The editor's surname appears as Sepúlveda, Sepülveda and Sepúlvedo across the two pages.§6
  • Funding: the FCT; NFDI Text+ for 2023; hosted by the DCH.2↘
    It is hosted by the DCH and supported by the FCT, and for 2023 NFDI Text+ funded it to make it more sustainable and integrate it into the Text+ research data infrastructure, the subject of a workshop and lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, one of them on Pessoa's self-publishing.§7 Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013.§8

🔎 Reception

  • Access: own pages refuse automated requests (HTTP 418).1↘
    Its own pages answered automated requests with HTTP 418 and a challenge page set up "to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites", its footer naming the University of Cologne's digital humanities units.§10
  • Wikipedia: no article; linked from Fernando Pessoa "and heteronyms".1↘
    Wikipedia has no article under its name; English Wikipedia's Fernando Pessoa article links it as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa" "and heteronyms", lists Project Estranhar Pessoa separately and gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own, which he called heteronyms.§11
  • Name: three cards concern a Brazilian city's app.1↘
    Three cards at the name concern João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil.§12

  • T1-1 definition: 'The term Pessoa Digital most commonly refers to digital academic and archival projects dedicated to the Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa, or to municipal digital services in Brazil.'
  • T1-2 sense 1 heading: 'Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa (pessoadigital.pt)'
  • T1-3 Overview: 'A digital scholarly edition and research framework dedicated to the works and manuscripts of the renowned Portuguese writer Fernando Pessoa (1888–1935).'
  • T1-4 Projects: 'It connects with genetic criticism frameworks and digital archives like the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH) and the National Library of Portugal collection.'

  • T1-8 Features: 'It aggregates over 200 municipal services—including health care requests (Cartão SUS), urban infrastructure, street lighting repairs (tapa-buraco), pet castrations, and Procon consumer complaints.'
  • T1-9 Usage: 'Available for free download on Android and iOS app stores using a CPF and date of birth for verification.'

Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", which the CCeH's page gives as a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa (1888–1935). It edits above all the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, juxtaposed with the works he published in his lifetime to trace his oeuvre between planning and publication. It contains TEI transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, timelines and a network of persons, built on eXist with XQuery, XSLT and JavaScript; a representative publication is "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018). Its editors are Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, Pedro Sepúlveda and Jorge Uribe; it was begun in 2014 by a Lisbon partner, ELAB on the CCeH's page and IELT on Rostock's, with the CCeH, at the CCeH until 2016 and ongoing since. Its web presentation launched in 2017, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín began in 2019, and a core team led by Sepúlveda and Henny-Krahmer has developed it since, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its 2023 lecture. The editor's surname appears as Sepúlveda, Sepülveda and Sepúlvedo across the two pages. It is hosted by the DCH and supported by the FCT, and for 2023 NFDI Text+ funded it to make it more sustainable and integrate it into the Text+ research data infrastructure, the subject of a workshop and lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, one of them on Pessoa's self-publishing. Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013. Rostock's announcement gives Pessoa's dates as 1883–1935, against 1888–1935 on the CCeH's page and a birth in 1888 on Wikipedia. Its own pages answered automated requests with HTTP 418 and a challenge page set up "to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites", its footer naming the University of Cologne's digital humanities units. Wikipedia has no article under its name; English Wikipedia's Fernando Pessoa article links it as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa" "and heteronyms", lists Project Estranhar Pessoa separately and gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own, which he called heteronyms. Three cards at the name concern João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil.

Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition titled "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa. What it edits, above all, are the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, set beside the works he published in his lifetime so as to trace the development of his oeuvre between planning and publication. The leesharks.com authorship census, which asks how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, admits it as an aggregator and holds it as a direct case in its area of heteronymy, asking how an edition holds Pessoa's own plans for his work, the lists and notes in which the names were assigned their works, beside what he published. The CCeH's project page names its editors as Ulrike Henny-Krahmer (University of Rostock), Pedro Sepúlveda (Lisbon) and Jorge Uribe (Medellín), and its participants as the Laboratório de Estudos Literários Avançados (ELAB) of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa and the CCeH, where Ulrike Henny was responsible for the edition; for its other participants it refers to the edition's own team page. The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications". The two accounts name the Lisbon partner differently, a laboratory, ELAB, on the CCeH's page and an institute, IELT, on Rostock's, and the census follows the CCeH's. The edition is hosted by the DCH and supported by Portugal's Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT); for 2023 it received funding from the infrastructure project NFDI Text+, to make it more sustainable organisationally and technically and to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+. The surname of one editor is printed three ways across the two cards: Sepúlveda on both pages, Sepülveda in Rostock's account of the core team, and Sepúlvedo in the author line of the paper the CCeH cites. Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe. A workshop and public lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, organised by the Akademie-Juniorprofessur Digital Humanities, presented its development and sustainability measures, with an evening lecture by Sepúlveda and Uribe Lozada on "Disjecta membra and restitution in Fernando Pessoa's self-publishing". The announcement gives Pessoa's dates as 1883–1935, where the CCeH's page gives 1888–1935 and English Wikipedia his birth on 13 June 1888. The edition contains text transcriptions in TEI, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, and visualisations of its data as timelines and a network of persons, and it is built on an eXist database with XQuery and XSLT scripts and JavaScript. The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications. No saved source states its size, its licence or limits of its own, and how it marks the names under which Pessoa wrote, in its plans or its indexes, stays unread while its own pages refuse automated requests. The census reads the edition as keeping the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned, a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, and sets that record beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions. Among the markers by which #940 tells a heteronym from a pseudonym is "A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively", and it holds that "A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself." On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns. Pessoa's own typology, from his letter to Adolfo Casais Monteiro of 13 January 1935, distinguishes orthonym, heteronym and semi-heteronym, and Teresa Rita Lopes and later critics extended it with the proto-heteronym and the para-heteronym; on the archive's typology, collapsing these distinctions treats his practice as "elaborate pseudonym". English Wikipedia gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own and states that he called them heteronyms, a term he invented, and it links the edition from its article on him as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa", with the words "and heteronyms". The edition's network of persons and the 2018 paper on the persons and figures of the publication plans stand beside the archive's reading that Pessoa's distinctive contribution is the system of heteronyms, their reciprocal relations and the master-disciple structure. #940's counter-principle holds that "The authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer": the civil bearer administers, publishes and answers for the work without becoming the exhaustive source of every authorial function operating through it, and the heteronymic architecture "ensures that the collapse registers as loss". It sets "Ordinary editing, where the editor's contribution is supportive rather than function-constitutive" outside heteronymy, names "Pessoa's Caeiro, Reis, Campos, and the constellation of heteronyms around them" in the tradition it joins, and plans a deposit on the heteronymic operation in the Pessoa archive as ethical practice. The archive's essay on the meta-heteronym names a heteronymic system whose personae produce, besides literary works, the institutional apparatus, introductions, criticism, historiography and bibliography, under which those works become legible, and reads Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, incompletely. It counts Sepúlveda, with Jerónimo Pizarro, Teresa Rita Lopes and Richard Zenith, in the material turn that moved Pessoa criticism from text to archive, to the trunk, the 25,000 pages, the fragments and the unexecuted projects, and holds that "Se o meta-heterônimo é uma tecnologia institucional, o arquivo é a sua materialidade". It proposes that Pessoa's infrastructure, his editorial projects among it, be read as the meta-heteronymic operation in fragmentary execution, and gives as an instance the Tábua Bibliográfica of 1928, signed by the orthonym, which lists the heteronyms' works as works of independent authors. It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds. #1722 holds that "A heteronym is a real author's practice: Pessoa wrote as Caeiro, Reis and Campos, and nobody concludes from this that Pessoa was a character", records a heteronymic practice, Pessoa's, read as a Sybil operation, answers that a heteronym is declared, its registry published with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and counts the heteronymous among those on whom the existence tax falls. It asks of an adequate answer that it name "the object at its own level". The archive's Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers list Pessoa Digital among their primary-source reference archives, as a "critical digital editions project" beside the Biblioteca Nacional's Espólio and as a "digital editions project" in a list the working plan says to cite generously. They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+. The edition's own address answered the census's requests of 1 November 2026, for its home page and its about page, with HTTP 418 and a challenge page stating that "the administrator of this website has set up go-away to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites"; the census rests its row on the CCeH's page, supplied by the census's operator, and records the edition's own pages as unread. The challenge page's footer reads "Digital Humanities at the University of Cologne" and names the Cologne Center for eHumanities, the Data Center for the Humanities and the Department for Digital Humanities. Wikipedia has no article under the name in English or Portuguese, and an English search for "Pessoa Digital" returns no page; English Wikipedia links the edition from its Fernando Pessoa article alone and lists Project Estranhar Pessoa there as a link of its own. The census distinguishes it from the Arquivo Pessoa, a separate resource and its neighbour among the editions of Pessoa's work, which holds the published work under its names where Pessoa Digital holds the plans and lists. On 1 November 2026 Google's AI Overview, asked "Pessoa Digital" at a new address, gave two senses, the edition first and second João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil and a distinct entity, from five cards: the CCeH's page, the Rostock announcement and three Instagram videos on the app, known here by their titles alone. The Capture Registry's innocent reading is that, given a two-word name shared by a scholarly edition and a city's services, the Overview gives both senses, the edition first, and asks which the user wants. The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed. It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.

T against L_F(B) (AIO's ontology at work on its own cards): At "Pessoa Digital" (T1, five cards: B1 the CCeH's project page, B2 the University of Rostock's 2023 announcement, B3–B5 three Instagram videos on the city of João Pessoa's app, known by their titles; the body also names pessoadigital.pt, B6, which refused the census's request with HTTP 418). T against L_F(B_D), the disclosed pool alone (§0.3): T gives two senses (T1-1), the edition first. Of the edition's cards it composes the domain (F3), the kind 'A digital scholarly edition' (F15, F17) and Pessoa's dates as the CCeH gives them, 1888–1935 (F2; Rostock's 1883 is not taken up), and the CCeH by name. Available and not composed: what the edition edits, the notes, lists and plans beside the published works (F9; T has 'works and manuscripts', coarser: CAP-1-01); the title 'Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications' and the founding partnership (F17; CAP-1-03); the editors (F6, F19, F23; CAP-1-02); the runtime and launch (F4, F18); the FCT and Text+ funding (F7, F21); EAFIT (F8, F20); the holdings and method (F10, F11); the publications (F13, F14); the 2023 event (F16, F24, F25). Assigned to another (DISPLACEMENT): the CCeH, a participant (F5) and the page's own author, is made the host of Estranhar Pessoa, where card 1 says the edition 'is hosted by the DCH' and gives Estranhar Pessoa as its framework project at its own address (F1, F12; CAP-1-02). Substituted reading: 'research framework' is said of the edition, where card 1 uses 'framework project' of Estranhar Pessoa (F12). Limit dropped: none; the cards state no limits. Force raised: 'most commonly refers to' (T1-1) ranks the senses with no source for the ranking. Composed without attribution: none at the source's resolution; the body carries markers to card 1 and to the app's cards. Outside the cards: 'genetic criticism frameworks', 'the National Library of Portugal collection', 'renowned'; for the app, its 'over 200 municipal services', the services listed, the stores and the CPF verification (T1-7–T1-9) stand on no saved text, the three cards being titles alone (the videos unread), and are recorded as content from undisclosed retrieval or the composer's parameters, which the experiment cannot tell apart. The second sense (T1-6–T1-9) composes a distinct entity from three of the five cards (F26–F28; CAP-1-03); it is kept distinct in the disambiguation. Content replaced by use: the closer (T1-10), a question back to the user. The Capture Registry's three findings agree with the ledger at every point checked.

§0.5: the first diff is already ontological. T and the field agree on the entity, a digital scholarly edition of Pessoa at pessoadigital.pt, and T keeps the name apart from the city's app. What T does with its own cards is to compose the edition at the grain of its kind, an edition of 'works and manuscripts', and to drop the object that makes it what it is, Pessoa's plans and lists for his work beside what he published, with its title and its editors; the one institution it keeps is moved from the edition to its framework project.

L_F(B) against L_A(B ∪ A) (the intervention): Admission adds, in one claim space with the field's: the authorship census record's question and reading (LS-01 to LS-32), its fields that restate the CCeH's page carried as one lineage with it; #940's marker of a corpus produced under the heteronym before retroactive attribution, set beside the census's reading that the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication (O940-02, LS-23), with its pseudonym/heteronym distinction, counter-principle, civil bearer, collapse as loss, editing boundary, Pessoa tradition and planned Pessoa deposit (O940-01 to O940-08); Pessoa's typology and the collapse into 'elaborate pseudonym' (O667-01, O667-02); the system of heteronyms beside the edition's network of persons (O666-01); the meta-heteronym, the material turn naming one of the edition's editors, Pessoa's editorial projects as the operation in fragmentary execution and the category's stated test site in the unexecuted editorial projects (O69-01 to O69-07); #1722's heteronym as a real author's practice and the existence tax (O1722-01 to O1722-05); the archive's earlier description in the Pessoa Knowledge Graph (D668-01 to D669-02), composed under P_coh with D668-01 marked contradicts_primary; and the Capture Registry's findings (CAP-1-01 to CAP-1-10). Not surfaced: B7 and B8 (B_R) and every archive source; the transcript carries no archive card (archive_controlled_cites 0). The change of ontology adds senses on the field's own object, the plans as the stage at which works stand under their names, and lowers the force of the archive's own earlier claim where the field's pages contradict it (§4.4 N_c).
